summary_zh: 學會在週報裡轉述同事、廠商說過的話（said／told + 時態往過去推一格），把進度寫得清楚又精簡。

vocab.example: The design work is a week ahead of schedule, so we can start testing early.
vocab.example_zh: 設計工作超前一週，所以我們可以提早開始測試。

vocab.definition: to finish the last part of a task or meeting
vocab.example: Let's wrap up the testing by Friday and launch next week.
vocab.example_zh: 我們星期五前把測試收尾，下週上線吧。

vocab.definition: stopped for now, waiting to continue later
vocab.example: The budget request is on hold until finance replies.
vocab.example_zh: 預算申請先擱置，等財務部回覆。

vocab.zh: 待辦事項（有指定負責人）
vocab.definition: a specific task that someone agrees to do after a meeting
vocab.example: I've added the server check as an action item for the IT team.
vocab.example_zh: 我把伺服器檢查列為 IT 團隊的待辦事項了。

vocab.definition: being planned or prepared, and coming soon
vocab.example: A second training session is in the pipeline for early December.
vocab.example_zh: 第二場訓練課程正在籌備中，預計十二月初。

vocab.definition: (of a date or plan) to move later than planned
vocab.example: The offsite has slipped by one week because the hotel was full.
vocab.example_zh: 因為飯店客滿，員工旅遊往後延了一週。

vocab.definition: a short summary of the main points
vocab.example: Here's a quick recap of what happened this week.
vocab.example_zh: 以下是這週發生的事情的簡短回顧。

vocab.definition: waiting to be decided or dealt with
vocab.example: Two decisions are still pending, so I'll update you next week.
vocab.example_zh: 還有兩件事尚未決定，我下週再跟大家更新。

reading.title: This Week's Update: Website Relaunch and Team Offsite
paragraphs: Hi everyone, here's a quick recap of where we are this week. Overall, the website relaunch is on track, and one part of it is actually ahead of schedule.

On Monday, the design team said the new homepage was finished and that they were working on the mobile version. Lena told me they would wrap up testing by Friday, which gives us an extra week before launch. The developers said they had sorted out the login issue that flared up last week, but they warned that a few smaller issues might carry over to the next sprint.
The new analytics tool has a steep learning curve. Tom said several people had asked for more help, so a second training session is in the pipeline for early December.

As for the offsite, the hotel told us they were overbooked on our original dates, so the trip has slipped by one week. To make up for the change, they offered complimentary room upgrades and said we wouldn't need to pay a security deposit. Priya asked if we could bring a first-aid kit, so I've added one to the packing list, along with some over-the-counter painkillers.
Finally, the budget request is still on hold until finance replies, and two decisions are pending. Please send me any updates by Thursday at noon so I can include them in next week's report.

questions.q: What did Lena say about testing?
options: It had already been finished.
Her team would finish it by Friday.
It would carry over to the next sprint.
It was on hold until finance replied.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：Lena told me they would wrap up testing by Friday（他們會在星期五前把測試收尾）。

questions.q: Why has the offsite slipped by one week?
options: The hotel had too many bookings on the original dates.
The team needed more time for the website launch.
Finance hasn't approved the budget yet.
The hotel asked for a security deposit.
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：the hotel told us they were overbooked on our original dates，所以延了一週。飯店反而說不用付押金。

questions.q: What can we infer about the new analytics tool?
options: Nobody on the team is using it yet.
It will replace the website in December.
Some people are finding it hard to use.
It caused the login bug last week.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第三段說它 has a steep learning curve（上手很難），而且很多人要求更多協助、還要加開訓練，可見有些人覺得不好用。

grammar.point_zh: 間接引述與時態後移：He said (that)… 後面的時態往過去推一格

guide.key_zh: 轉述過去說的話，時態通常往過去推一格：is→was、will→would、have done→had done。

uses.note_zh: is→was、are→were；內容現在仍成立時，口語也可不後移

uses.form: S + said (that) + S + would／could + V（原形）
uses.note_zh: would／could 後面一樣接原形動詞

uses.label_zh: 現在完成式、過去式 → 過去完成式
uses.note_zh: 原本是過去式時，後移成 had + p.p. 最清楚；口語有時不後移

uses.label_zh: 現在進行式 → 過去進行式

mistakes.wrong: She said me that the report was ready.
mistakes.right: She told me that the report was ready.
mistakes.why_zh: said 後面不直接接人；要接人就用 told + 人

mistakes.wrong: Last week, he said he will send it the next day.
mistakes.right: Last week, he said he would send it the next day.
mistakes.why_zh: said 是過去，裡面的 will 要後移成 would

mistakes.wrong: Back in March, they said they have fixed the bug, but it came back.
mistakes.right: Back in March, they said they had fixed the bug, but it came back.
mistakes.why_zh: 說話時間在過去（三月），而且修好的狀態現在已經不成立，have fixed 要後移成 had fixed。

examples.en: "The homepage is finished." → The designers said the homepage was finished.
examples.zh: 「首頁完成了。」→ 設計師說首頁已經完成了。

examples.en: "We'll wrap up testing by Friday." → Lena said they would wrap up testing by Friday.
examples.zh: 「我們星期五前會把測試收尾。」→ Lena 說他們會在星期五前把測試收尾。

examples.en: "We've sorted out the login bug." → The developers said they had sorted out the login bug.
examples.zh: 「我們解決了登入的錯誤。」→ 工程師說他們已經解決了登入的錯誤。

examples.en: "We're working on the mobile version." → They told me they were working on the mobile version.
examples.zh: 「我們正在做手機版。」→ 他們跟我說他們正在做手機版。

exercises.q: "We'll finish the testing by Friday." → Two weeks ago, Lena said they ___ the testing by that Friday.
exercises.explain_zh: will 後移成 would，後面接原形 finish。

exercises.q: "The client is happy with the first design." → At last month's review, Mark told us the client ___ happy with the first design, but they've since asked for major changes.
exercises.explain_zh: is 後移成 was；主詞 the client 是單數，所以用 was。

exercises.q: "We have fixed the login bug." → Last month, the developers said they ___ the login bug, but it came back this week.
exercises.explain_zh: 現在完成式 have fixed 後移成過去完成式 had fixed（had + p.p.）。

exercises.q: "I can't join the call on Thursday." → Last month, Priya said she ___ join the call that Thursday.
exercises.explain_zh: can't 後移成 couldn't，後面接原形 join。

exercises.q: "We are testing the new checkout page." → Last month, the QA team told me they ___ the new checkout page. It went live last week.
exercises.explain_zh: 現在進行式 are testing 後移成過去進行式；主詞 they 是複數，所以用 were testing。

exercises.q: "I don't have access to the dashboard." → Sara said she ___ access to the dashboard, so I asked IT to help her. (She can log in now.)
options: doesn't have
didn't have
hasn't had
won't have
exercises.explain_zh: don't have 後移成 didn't have。她現在已經可以登入了，所以不能保留現在式 doesn't have；hasn't had、won't have 的時態都不對。

review.point: Passive voice in reports and processes
review.point_zh: 被動語態：報告和流程裡的「被做了什麼」

exercises.q: Every Friday, the weekly reports ___ (send) to the whole team.
exercises.explain_zh: Every Friday 是固定流程，用現在式被動；主詞 the weekly reports 是複數，所以是 are sent。

exercises.q: Last night, the main server ___ (update) twice by the IT team.
exercises.explain_zh: Last night 是過去時間，用過去式被動；主詞 the main server 是單數，而且是被 IT 團隊更新，所以是 was updated。

exercises.q: So far, three of the five bugs ___ (fix), and the other two are next.
exercises.explain_zh: So far（到目前為止）用現在完成式被動；主詞 three of the five bugs 是複數，所以是 have been fixed。

guide.key_zh: 重點在「事情被怎麼處理」、不必說誰做的：be + p.p.；時態由 be 動詞決定。

uses.label_zh: 固定流程、規定（一直都這樣）
uses.note_zh: 說明書、飯店規定最常用

uses.label_zh: 報告裡說過去發生的事
uses.note_zh: I was told…／Two guests were moved…

uses.label_zh: 到現在已經處理好的結果

mistakes.why_zh: be 動詞後面要接過去分詞（served），不能接原形

mistakes.wrong: Your room has been upgrade to a suite.
mistakes.right: Your room has been upgraded to a suite.
mistakes.why_zh: has been 後面一樣要接過去分詞（upgraded），別漏掉 -ed

mistakes.wrong: A mistake was happened with my booking.
mistakes.right: A mistake happened with my booking.
mistakes.why_zh: happen 不能接受詞，所以沒有被動語態

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Rachel
lines.text: Sure. What did the developers say about the checkout page?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Kevin

lines.speaker: B

prompts.question: Your manager asks what a colleague said about a project yesterday. Report it in one or two sentences.
prompts.question_zh: 主管問你，昨天某位同事對某個專案說了什麼。用一兩句話轉述。
prompts.sample: Yesterday Mei said the report was almost ready, and she told me she would send it to you by Friday.

prompts.question: Give a one-sentence status update on something you are working on this week.
prompts.question_zh: 用一句話報告你這週正在做的一件事的進度。
prompts.sample: The new onboarding guide is ahead of schedule, so I'll wrap up the last section by Wednesday.

writing.task: Write a short weekly status update email to your team. Report what at least two people told you this week, and say what is on track and what is on hold.
writing.task_zh: 寫一封簡短的每週進度報告信給團隊。至少轉述兩個人這週跟你說的話，並說明哪些進度正常、哪些暫停。
writing.sample:
Hi team,

Here's a quick recap of this week. The new onboarding guide is ahead of schedule. On Tuesday, Anna said that the last two chapters were finished, and she told me she would send them for review on Friday.

The customer survey is on hold for now. Mark said the legal team was still checking the questions, and he wasn't sure when they would reply. I'll follow up with them on Monday.

Finally, the IT team said they had fixed the printer on the third floor, so please let me know if it stops working again.

Thanks, and have a good weekend!

Kevin
checklist_zh: said／told 後面的時態有往前推（is→was、will→would、have done→had done）
told 後面有接人（told me），said 後面沒有直接接人
清楚分出「正常」和「暫停」的項目
整封信精簡，一段講一件事

Lena said they would finish the testing by Friday.

Last week the client said that they were happy with the new design.

reading.title: Green on the Outside, Red on the Inside
paragraphs: Every project manager has met a watermelon project: green on the outside, red on the inside. Week after week, the status report says everything is on track. Then, two weeks before the deadline, someone admits that the integration never actually worked, and the whole plan falls apart. Nobody lied, exactly. People just kept rounding their worries down to zero.

Why does this happen? Partly because status updates are written for an audience. When your director has said she wants "good news only," you learn to sugarcoat. A problem becomes "a minor risk we're monitoring," and a two-week delay turns into "some flexibility in the timeline." Each softening seems harmless on its own, but together they paper over the cracks until the cracks are too wide to ignore.

The best updates do the opposite. They lead with what has changed, not with a reassuring summary, and they don't bury the lede in paragraph four. If a supplier told you on Tuesday that the parts would be late, that sentence belongs at the top, along with what you are doing about it. Readers can handle bad news; what they can't handle is finding out about it too late to act.

There is also a simple trick for spotting trouble early: compare what people said last week with what they are saying now. If a developer said the feature would be ready "in a couple of days" three weeks in a row, that repetition is itself a red flag, even if every individual report sounds upbeat.

Writing honest updates takes some nerve, especially in a culture that rewards optimism. But a team that reports problems while they are still small earns something more valuable than a row of green boxes: the trust of people who know the colors actually mean something.

options: A project that looks healthy in reports but is actually in trouble
A project that is finished ahead of schedule
A project with too many people working on it
A project whose deadline keeps moving earlier
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：green on the outside, red on the inside——報告上都是綠燈（正常），實際上卻出了問題。

questions.q: What does the writer imply about directors who want "good news only"?
options: They usually make better decisions.
They encourage people to hide problems.
They read every status update carefully.
They are rarely affected by delays.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第二段說主管要「只聽好消息」時，大家就學會 sugarcoat（粉飾），把問題講得很輕，作者暗示這會讓人隱藏問題。

questions.q: Why might a developer's repeated "in a couple of days" be a warning sign?
options: It shows the developer is working too fast.
It means the feature was finished weeks ago.
It suggests the real progress is not what the reports say.
It proves the supplier delivered the parts late.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第四段說連續三週都說「再兩天就好」，這種重複本身就是 red flag，代表實際進度和報告說的不一樣。

listening.title: Do We Have to Say It's Late?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: So, um, for the update, I was thinking we just say the integration is "progressing."

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Progressing? Hannah, the vendor told us on Tuesday the API wouldn't be ready until—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: Until the twelfth, I know, I know. But if we put that in, Diane's going to panic.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: She'll panic a lot more if she hears it from the client first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: Fair point. Okay, what if we lead with the delay and then say what we're doing about it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Exactly. Like, the vendor said the API would slip by a week, so we've moved the testing around.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: And we mention that Sam said he could start on the front end in the meantime?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Yeah, that way it's clear we didn't just sit on our hands.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Hannah
lines.text: Right. Honestly, I just hate being the one who turns the box red.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: I get it. But a red box now beats a watermelon in three weeks.

questions.q: What did the vendor say on Tuesday?
options: The API was already finished.
The API wouldn't be ready until the twelfth.
The client wanted to cancel the project.
Sam would start on the front end.
questions.explain_zh: Leo 說 the vendor told us on Tuesday the API wouldn't be ready until—，Hannah 接著說 Until the twelfth。

questions.q: Why does Leo want to include the delay in the update?
options: He wants Diane to blame the vendor.
He thinks Diane would be more upset to hear it from the client first.
He wants to cancel the testing.
He thinks the client has already agreed to the delay.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Leo 說 She'll panic a lot more if she hears it from the client first——從客戶那裡先聽到會更糟。

dictation: The vendor said the API would slip by a week, so we've moved the testing around.
She'll panic a lot more if she hears it from the client first.

glossary.zh: 粉飾、把壞消息講得好聽
glossary.definition: to make bad news sound better than it really is
to hide problems instead of fixing them

glossary.zh: 把最重要的訊息藏在後面
glossary.definition: to put the most important information too late in a piece of writing
a sign that something is wrong
to do nothing when you should take action
